_comment: Product introduction (01_Produktove_video.mp4). HELD: not published. Two narration lines conflict with release 1.0.3.6 (INSTALL.pdf section 9a: excerpts are the AI's reading, 'not copied from the file and not checked against it'; 'the extraction can miss or misread a clause'), and the SharePoint and Wording/Calculation/Review slides show an empty box where an arrow glyph failed to render. English transcript only; translations follow the corrected master. The 'conflict' field marks the lines that must change.

segments.en: An auto-renewing contract needs only one missed notice date to lock you in for another year.
And that date is usually buried in a schedule, an amendment or the small print.
Contract Intelligence & Register from ColleagueAI runs inside your own Microsoft 365 tenant.
It reads the contracts in your SharePoint library, extracts the key terms with a quote to the source, and sends every extraction to a named reviewer in Teams.
segments.conflict: 'with a quote to the source': 1.0.3.6 presents excerpts as the AI's unverified reading, not as quotations. Proposed: 'extracts the key terms with the excerpt it relied on'.

segments.en: Here, a master services agreement is uploaded.
The reviewer sees each term with its quote: the notice period exactly as written, every notice clause found in the document, and the signing date.
segments.conflict: 'exactly as written' and the on-screen 'Every notice clause found': the extraction can miss or misread a clause (INSTALL 9a: 'six (6) months' read as '90 (90) months'). Proposed: 'The reviewer sees each term with the AI's excerpt, to check against the contract: the notice period, the notice clauses it found, and the signing date.'

segments.en: One click approves it, and the register records who approved it and when.
When clauses conflict, it doesn't guess.
This contract says three months in the main text and six months in the small print, so the deadline is held back.
The reviewer reads the source, confirms six months, and only then does the deadline appear.
Now your team can ask the agent which notice deadlines fall in the next 90 days, and see the wording and the calculation behind each one.
People outside the team see nothing.
It runs in your tenant, and a person approves every result.
